summary: world.zones implemented end to end: 8 m world-aligned cell grid, a buildable band derived from world.roads.frontage (depth 1-4 cells, nearest road wins, cells rejected on water, >24 deg slope / >6.5 m relief per cell and road coverage), paint/erase brushes with a batched bulk() path, version bump + zones:changed with real added/removed lot deltas, and lot generation along every frontage (16-32 m wide, 16-32 m deep, corner-fitted, claim-based so a block subdivides as a pinwheel instead of mitred quadrants; lot ids and buildingId survive a rebuild). Overlay is a CS2-style decal: one merged terrain-conforming mesh per zone type (saturated translucent fill, dark 8 m grid, 45 deg hatch on high density, animated bright region outline), one mesh for the empty zonable band and one for lot outlines with a frontage bar - 6 draw calls, 21.9k triangles, polygonOffset + depthWrite off, unlit with fog and AgX tonemapping so it reads the same day and night. Visible when a zoning tool is active (tool:changed, with a fade) or always in the showcase. Showcase stages a 7x5 street grid with an avenue, a diagonal, a curved street and two alleys, then paints all four types in both densities on both sides of every road, leaving two blocks unzoned so the empty band shows; camera presets zones / zonesclose / zoneswide.
remainingWeaknesses: The fill still reads a little flat/plasticky at street and closeup range: it is a single translucent colour over the ground with a grid, where CS2 also varies the overlay per cell state (hover, blocked, newly painted).

Lot subdivision is irregular in places. The claim order is deterministic but jittered per edge, so some frontages get a full row of 3 lots and the perpendicular street only gets one 16 m 'flag' lot in the middle of the block; a couple of short frontages get none at all.
'Corner lots merged' is implemented as a 3 m extension of the first/last lot toward the junction, not as a true L-shaped lot with frontage on both roads.
The high/low density distinction relies on hue plus a faint 45 deg hatch; at aerial distance the hatch is nearly invisible, so density reads mostly from colour.
No brush/hover preview cell highlight (that belongs to the tools module, but zoning exposes no highlight hook for it yet).
8 m cells are world-aligned per the contract, so along curved or diagonal streets the band edge staircases instead of following the road like CS2's per-road cell grid.
The animated outline pulse is slow and subtle; it is invisible in stills and only reads in motion.
The overlay does not dim at night, which is correct for a UI decal but makes the night aerial shots read brighter than the terrain.
